climateNote: This is a volcano-mechanics event: magma pressure pushing the south flank seaward along a deep fault. No climate connection is claimed — it is included for the descending-pass radar physics lesson.

dataset.mission: Sentinel-1A/1B (Copernicus), descending pass; historical ALOS/ENVISAT in published studies
dataset.datasetId: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory GNSS + InSAR; Copernicus Sentinel-1 SLC
dataset.window: Published: multi-year flank creep record; in-app pass-pair window: 1,080 days
dataset.coverage: Kīlauea south flank, Hawaiʻi (~70 km scene)
dataset.gnss: UWEV + AHUP, Nevada Geodetic Lab daily IGS20 solutions, bundled as weekly means
dataset.processing: Published: HVO GNSS/inSAR monitoring and flank-creep studies. In-app: elastic flank-slide model; one fringe = λ/2 line-of-sight motion

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: Real daily IGS20 solutions from NGL stations UWEV and AHUP, downsampled to weekly means, bundled and charted in-app.

items.label: MEASURED
items.detail: Up to ~10 cm/yr seaward flank motion (USGS HVO); M 6.9 south-flank earthquake 4 May 2018 (USGS). Shown as citations; not re-derived in-app.

items.label: MODELED
items.detail: Physics rendering of the elastic flank model (peak 27 cm over 1,080 days). NOT a raw SAR image — computed on-device.

items.label: DERIVED
items.detail: Computed on-device from the physical model (one fringe = λ/2 LOS). Tracks the model, not a downloaded product.

items.label: LIVE
items.detail: Live accelerometer from the demo ESP32 ground station — IoT demo at the demo site; not a satellite measurement of this event.

limitations: The interferogram is a physics rendering of published figures, not raw SAR pixels — no SAR processing is done in-app.
Flank creep is episodic; the steady model under-represents rupture-driven jumps like May 2018.
Descending-pass look geometry makes the scene sensitive to along-track ionosphere in real data.
